fields.h1: Build a Library Survey Your Patrons Finish
fields.hero_description: Build a library survey patrons answer on any phone, with every response saved to a database your library owns.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Library Survey
fields.features_subheading: Describe your patrons and the decision ahead, and Emergent builds the survey they answer and the table that holds every response.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for your patrons

Tell Emergent who uses the library and what the board has to decide, such as weekend hours. Emergent drafts questions to fit, and a follow-up prompt rewords or cuts any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Answers kept apart from names

Ask for an anonymous survey, and each answer is saved with no name or card number beside it. Staff read the totals and every comment without knowing which patron wrote which one.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

Patrons scan a QR code at a table or tap the link in an email, then answer one question per screen. Emergent sets no cap on responses, so a busy branch never closes the survey early.
fields.feature_4:
Every response in a database you own

Each response is a row in a database the library owns, tagged with the branch and the date. Put this year's answers beside last year's when the board reviews hours or study space.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts when a score drops

Pick a question and a threshold, such as a quiet rating below 3 out of 5. When the average falls under it, the app emails the branch manager the score and a link to the comments.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your code

Run the survey on the library's own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and reuse it next year.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Library Surveys and What Changed
fields.tab_content_1:
Sunday hours, which 263 cardholders asked for

Fenwick Falls Public Library has always closed on Sundays, and the board wanted to know if it should. The library emailed its 2,400 cardholders a survey listing four time slots when the doors are shut. Of the 612 who answered, 263 picked Sunday afternoon. Starting in March, the library opens on Sundays, 1 to 5 pm.
fields.tab_content_2:
Second floor goes silent before finals after a 2.4 for quiet

Dellmont College library runs short of quiet seats in exam weeks. A QR code on each study table opens a 3-question survey that rates the quiet on that floor out of 5. A floor averaging below 3 emails the library dean. The second floor averaged 2.4 across 418 ratings and became a silent floor for finals week.
fields.tab_content_3:
Graphic novels or fantasy? Novels win with 141 votes

Each semester, the Tamsin Hill Middle School librarian asks students what they want on the shelves. They open the link on a phone or school laptop, and no names are saved. This spring 296 answered: 141 for graphic novels, 82 for fantasy. Of the $1,200 spring book order, $600 went to graphic novels.
fields.tab_content_4:
Laptop lending makes it into the 2027 plan

Orrin County Library wanted residents who never come in to shape its 2027 strategic plan. Links went up at all 5 branches and in the county newsletter, and 1,140 residents answered, each tagged by branch. At Eastgate, 88 of 210 asked for laptops to borrow, and the board wrote laptop lending into the plan.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a library survey?

plan.angle: The top 10 for library survey is government pages about the annual Public Libraries Survey that libraries file with their state, plus one how-to guide on user surveys and a strategic-planning guide. None shows a library building its own survey of patrons, students or residents and acting on the answers. This page is for that librarian: four library surveys built from a prompt and run to a decision (weekend hours at a public library, quiet seats at a college library, a middle school reading survey, a county needs survey for a strategic plan), a how-to on writing questions patrons finish, and an FAQ that separates the patron survey from the state statistics report.
tab_stories: Fenwick Falls Public Library emails 2,400 cardholders a survey on which closed hours they would use, 612 answer, 263 of 612 pick Sunday afternoon, and the library opens Sundays from 1 to 5 pm starting in March.

Dellmont College library puts a QR code on every study table, 418 students rate quiet on each floor from their phones, the second floor averages 2.4 of 5, which emails the library dean, and the second floor becomes a silent floor for finals week.

The Tamsin Hill Middle School librarian asks students what they want to read with no names saved, 296 answer, 141 of 296 pick graphic novels, and $600 of the $1,200 spring book order goes to graphic novels.

Orrin County Library runs a community survey for its 2027 strategic plan through links at 5 branches and the county newsletter, 1,140 residents answer, laptop lending tops the Eastgate branch with 88 of 210, and the board writes laptop lending into the plan.
